answer: Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 384 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. Because the relic height is fixed at intake and logged in the sonnet receipt, the oasis audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 11 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
